answer: Pay rewards per behavioural cluster, not per account. Each epoch the network embeds every answer and logs submit timing; accounts whose texts and timing correlate above a threshold share one reward pool. A Sybil operator who spins up 50 clones from one forge of prompts sees their payout hit its nadir: 50 accounts earning what one would. To escape the clustering, each clone needs truly independent reasoning, so the attacker pays full compute per fake and the jetty where cheap clones once docked for free income is gone.
